## Paper limitations

### [ExCyTIn-Bench](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.14201) (`arxiv-2507.14201`)

- constructed from single fictional Azure tenant
- questions derived from security tables (graph-based) may bias toward alert-centric investigation
- SQL-only interaction (no GUI/tools beyond querying)

### [Splunk SOC triage](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.23966) (`arxiv-2603.23966`)

- Fixed 5-minute windows can miss short-lived attacks
- Binary action space (Allow/Contain) only; no monitor/throttle/escalate
- No RAG or vector store; context management is funneling-only
- No retry or fallback logic documented for LLM or SPL failures
- Read-only by design; all mitigation executed by humans (intentional)
- Dataset scale and diversity limited; single-attacker simulation
- Local-LLM accuracy and hallucination risk untested

### [Cyber Defense Benchmark](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.19533) (`arxiv-2604.19533`)

- Several models are evaluated with a single rollout despite high LLM nondeterminism; the authors recommend multi-rollout averaging.
- All attack telemetry is Windows-only; Linux auditd, cloud telemetry, and network-flow hunting are not covered.
- Only 500 synthetic benign Sysmon EventID-1 records are injected, far below production SOC noise volume.
- Exact timestamp matching is intentionally strict and does not award partial credit for coarse but useful investigative localization.
- All evaluated hunters are zero-shot; trained or retrieval-augmented agents are outside this version's evaluation.
- The campaign generator is proprietary, although pre-built campaign data and full hunt traces are released.

### [LLM agents for vuln discovery](https://doi.org/10.1109/ACCESS.2026.3707573) (`doi-10.1109/ACCESS.2026.3707573`)

- CTF benchmarks do not equal production (authorization, rate limits, ambiguous success)
- Hallucination documented: invented file paths, misread forms, inferred nonexistent control flow
- Indirect prompt injection via untrusted page and log content; tool, memory, and RAG poisoning
- Containment imperfect in practice (shared kernels, metadata services; Clinejection incident hit ~4,000 developers)
- Context limits and lost-in-the-middle; retrieval failures can omit crucial evidence
- Reasoning-class model costs 5-20x per token
- Dual-use: scoped defensive prompts trivially repurposable

### [Agentic IoT security survey](https://doi.org/10.3390/electronics15122740) (`doi-10.3390/electronics15122740`)

- The paper is a systematic survey plus reference scaffold, not one empirically validated end-to-end security architecture.
- The shipped harness validation uses a deterministic stub rather than an LLM agent, so its scores cannot be treated as agent capability evidence.
- The synthetic-to-real negative control shows a major generalization gap (0.78 to 0.06 accuracy).
- Real-model evaluation across accuracy, latency, robustness, and prompt injection is deferred to staged future validation.
- The survey literature is heterogeneous across datasets, attack taxonomies, and deployment assumptions, limiting direct quantitative comparison.

### [LLM core agent survey](https://doi.org/10.4114/intartif.vol29iss78pp59-83) (`doi-10.4114/intartif.vol29iss78pp59-83`)

- Systematic review, so no implementation or artifacts of its own
- Heterogeneous metrics across surveyed studies limit direct comparison
- Rare TTPs under-recalled (18-32% missed)
- Prompt injection, data poisoning (1-5%), and poor confidence calibration remain exploitable
- Benchmark-to-production gap; few longitudinal operational SOC deployments
- Fine-tuning cost (tens of thousands of USD for GPT-3-class models) and RAG latency (2-5x)

### Agentic Reasoning Survey (`todo-agentic-reasoning`)

- Survey, not a system
- No empirical validation

### Org-Scoped LLM Runtime (`todo-org-scoped-runtime`)

- Architectural proposal; no production validation
- Evaluation plan not executed
- Several capabilities treated as extension paths

### [GenDFIR](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.02572) (`arxiv-2409.02572`)

- Evaluation uses synthetic, controlled incident scenarios rather than a production SOC or legal-forensics workload.
- The authors state that GenDFIR should not be treated as a universal DFIR solution and that results may not generalize beyond the tested configuration.
- Ground-truth checking and relevance assessment rely on a custom evaluation procedure rather than a broadly standardized DFIR benchmark.
- RAG can ground answers in incident evidence but does not itself guarantee forensic provenance, chain of custody, or hallucination-free conclusions.
- The fixed retrieval pipeline cannot autonomously decide to launch new telemetry queries when the retrieved context is insufficient.

### [Fine-tuned DApp vuln detector](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.05006) (`arxiv-2504.05006`)

- The dataset is specific to Solidity/DApp security, so transfer to operating-system, network, or SOC threat-hunting telemetry is not established.
- The key token-price-manipulation evaluation contains only 23 vulnerable contracts, limiting confidence for that rare logical-flaw class.
- Random over-sampling duplicates minority examples and can increase overfitting risk even when it improves class balance.
- The inference pipeline has no retrieval or external verification tool, so correctness remains dependent on the specialized model and verifier prompt.
- LoRA is cheaper but underperforms full-parameter fine-tuning in the reported experiments, exposing an accuracy-versus-training-cost trade-off.

### [CyberAgentX](https://doi.org/10.29121/DigiSecForensics.v2.i1.2025.86) (`doi-10.29121/DigiSecForensics.v2.i1.2025.86`)

- No prompts, code, or artifacts published despite claiming a reproducible methodology
- No hallucination guardrails described
- Autonomous SOAR execution without a documented sandbox or read-only API posture
- Black-box decision pathways; only 72% analyst trust even after SHAP/counterfactual exposure
- Adversarial robustness untested; the paper's own literature review reports 78% of tested LLM defense policies bypassable via jailbreaks
- Memory and retrieval strategy undefined

### [Multi-Agent LLM Threat Correlation](https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/document/3602681/) (`todo-ieee-access-2025-3602681`)

- legacy benchmark datasets may not reflect newest attack vectors
- API/tool dependencies introduce latency/single points of failure
- LLM explanations depend on prompt/model consistency
- synthetic validation data not fully public

### LLM for NIDS Survey (`todo-llm-nids-survey`)

- Survey only
- Challenges: validity (hallucination), complexity (compute), privacy

### LLM Vulnerability Detection Survey (`todo-vuln-detect-survey`)

- Survey only; no new method
- Dataset limitations: data leakage, narrow scope
- Lack of repository-level evaluation

### [ReAct](https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.03629) (`arxiv-2210.03629`)

- Performance depends on quality of in-context examples
- Struggles with large action spaces and long horizons
- Requires manual annotation of reasoning traces for few-shot prompts

### [Toolformer](https://arxiv.org/abs/2302.04761) (`arxiv-2302.04761`)

- Cannot chain tools
- Not interactive (no multi-turn tool use)
- Sample-inefficient for some APIs
- Sensitive to prompt wording

### [Reflexion](https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.11366) (`arxiv-2303.11366`)

- Relies on LLM's self-evaluation capability
- Can get stuck in local minima
- Limited long-term memory window
- Self-generated tests can be flaky

## Our avoid and open-question notes

### [GenDFIR](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.02572) (`arxiv-2409.02572`)

**Avoid**

- Treating strong synthetic-scenario scores as proof that the same design will work on noisy enterprise telemetry.
- Allowing generated narrative to become the forensic source of truth without preserving the underlying event provenance.

**Open questions**

- Should our retrieval store contain raw events, normalized Wazuh/Zeek records, investigation summaries, or all three?
- Should the hunter first perform active telemetry queries and then invoke fixed RAG, or should both evidence sources be available every step?
- How do we cite retrieved event IDs and source indices inside every generated finding?

### [Fine-tuned DApp vuln detector](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.05006) (`arxiv-2504.05006`)

**Avoid**

- Making fine-tuning the MVP dependency before we have our own representative telemetry and labels.
- Using duplicated oversampled examples as a substitute for collecting broader real attack evidence.
- Assuming a model specialized to one domain will transfer to Windows, Linux, and network threat hunting without evaluation.

**Open questions**

- Can our future hunt traces become supervised examples for a specialized model without leaking evaluation data?
- Would LoRA provide enough benefit on our telemetry, or would prompting/RAG/tool-use give better returns for less training cost?
- Should the verifier be another LLM pass or a deterministic evidence-checking component over Wazuh/Zeek results?

### [Splunk SOC triage](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.23966) (`arxiv-2603.23966`)

**Avoid**

- Fixed 5-minute windows (we use adaptive windows)
- Binary Allow/Contain action space (we add Monitor)
- No-RAG, funneling-only context (v2 adds RAG behind an interface)

**Open questions**

- Adaptive window sizing rules for short-lived attacks?
- How to map the priority score onto analyst queue ordering?

### [Cyber Defense Benchmark](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.19533) (`arxiv-2604.19533`)

**Avoid**

- Using exact timestamp submission as the only production success criterion; our system should also preserve evidence and attribution quality.
- Assuming an SQL-only, no-RAG tool surface is sufficient once we add CTI, ATT&CK knowledge, and heterogeneous Wazuh/Zeek telemetry.
- Treating current frontier LLMs as safe for unsupervised deployment; the benchmark explicitly shows they miss most malicious events.

**Open questions**

- How should the UniversalHunter query loop map to Wazuh/OpenSearch and Zeek instead of a single SQLite table?
- Should our evaluator score event recall, ATT&CK-step coverage, evidence quality, or a weighted combination?
- Do we evaluate open-ended hunts only, or also alert-seeded investigations where the agent pivots from one known signal?

### [LLM agents for vuln discovery](https://doi.org/10.1109/ACCESS.2026.3707573) (`doi-10.1109/ACCESS.2026.3707573`)

**Avoid**

- Offensive tool-first v1 (we start defensive)
- CTF-only benchmark metrics (we use the four-tier framework plus cost/regret)

**Open questions**

- Which of its benchmarks (Cybench, NYU CTF, AgentDojo) could run in evaluation against our defensive stack?
- How to bridge the benchmark-to-production gap in our eval harness?

### [CyberAgentX](https://doi.org/10.29121/DigiSecForensics.v2.i1.2025.86) (`doi-10.29121/DigiSecForensics.v2.i1.2025.86`)

**Avoid**

- Full, unsandboxed SOAR execution autonomy (we keep read-only defaults plus human approval)
- Opaque decision pathways without evidence references (analyst trust was only 72%)
- Documenting a framework without publishing prompts or code (reproducible: no)

**Open questions**

- How to budget the critic so the reflection loop cannot spin forever?
- Which ATT&CK-stage containment granularity maps cleanly onto our adaptive windows?

### [Agentic IoT security survey](https://doi.org/10.3390/electronics15122740) (`doi-10.3390/electronics15122740`)

**Avoid**

- Treating an illustrative reference scaffold as if it were already a validated production architecture.
- Using synthetic or deterministic-stub results as evidence that an LLM hunter works on real SOC telemetry.

**Open questions**

- Do we need one hunter agent first, or a coordinator with specialized investigation, CTI, and response agents?
- Where should persistent memory live, and how do we prevent memory or message-bus poisoning?
- Which actions stay read-only, and which require explicit analyst approval?

### [LLM core agent survey](https://doi.org/10.4114/intartif.vol29iss78pp59-83) (`doi-10.4114/intartif.vol29iss78pp59-83`)

**Avoid**

- Single-agent reference design (we use role-separated multi-agent)
- Expensive full fine-tuning as the default

**Open questions**

- How to operationalize confidence calibration in our L3 gate?
- Which TTP-sequence-annotated benchmark can serve as ground truth for hunt evaluation?
